headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: dexter’s broad network/API access can feed sensitive financial context into transformers’ file-and-browser pipeline without default verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can ingest external market/web content via Exa/Tavily and broad network egress, while transformers can read files and run browsers. If dexter’s outputs are copied into transformers’ inputs or shared files, prompt-like content can steer downstream processing. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not higher.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are placed into a shared file or browser-visible page that transformers reads
IF transformers treats file or browser content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable browser-driven ingestion for transformers
Require a human review step before copying dexter outputs
Prefix imported content as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; transformers has broad network egress and can read/write files. In a shared workspace, sensitive data can flow from dexter into transformers and then out through its networked processing. The pair’s interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or scratch directory
IF dexter stores financial data in files that transformers can read
IF transformers forwards file contents to remote services or model endpoints
mitigations: Isolate each agent in a separate directory
Block transformers from reading dexter scratch files
Restrict outbound network for one agent during handoff
Redact financial data before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while transformers can spawn subprocesses, install packages, and write files. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite artifacts or race on shared files. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the conflict is plausible in default multi-agent use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF dexter runs multiple instances concurrently
IF transformers installs packages or rewrites files in that workspace
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock
Run package installation only in a disposable environment
Snapshot the workspace before each agent run
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can autonomously produce research outputs from external APIs, and transformers can consume files, run browsers, and execute subprocesses. If transformers treats dexter’s outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into further processing or actions. Because no verification step is documented, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF transformers ingests dexter-generated reports without independent verification
IF downstream scripts or browser actions are triggered from those reports
mitigations: Require source checks before transformers acts on dexter output
Add a human approval gate for any downstream action
Keep dexter outputs read-only until reviewed
Compare outputs against original API responses
requires-engineering: implement validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly handles financial data and market data and requests multiple API keys, while transformers touches broad multimodal content and has broad network egress. If regulated financial data is routed into transformers’ general-purpose processing or external calls, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed by transformers outside the originating compliance boundary
IF logs or model calls retain that data beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of transformers inputs
Mask account or transaction identifiers before processing
Review retention settings for both agents
Limit logging of prompts and outputs
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing
